wrist_block/PMC13301753_jcm-15-04843-f00.title: Shear Wave Elastography in Musculoskeletal Imaging: A Narrative Review
wrist_block/PMC13301753_jcm-15-04843-f00.caption: Schematic overview of musculoskeletal applications and interpretation limits of shear wave elastography (SWE). SWE has been investigated in tendons and ligaments, skeletal muscles, peripheral nerves, menisci, cartilage, plantar fascia, and selected soft tissue lesions. Its potential clinical roles include adjunctive diagnosis, severity assessment, treatment monitoring, rehabilitation follow-up, and biomechanical biomarker development. Interpretation should consider tissue anisotropy, loading condition, probe pressure, ROI placement, measurement depth, and inter-vendor variability.

The needle, introduced in-plane from lateral to medial, is directed toward the pericapsular plane between the iliopsoas tendon and the pubic ramus. This setup corresponds to the standard ultrasound-guided PENG block technique performed by the anesthesiologist.
